title: Too Convinced to Stop
lines: Too Convinced to Stop asks how ambitious beliefs can remain answerable to evidence.
The book judges the process before success or failure rewrites the story.
It follows founders and institutions through confidence, authority, dissent, and the distribution of costs.
Its category of impossible certainty is explicitly nonclinical.
Readers gain questions for distinguishing bold experimentation from organizational protection against correction.

title: Evidence can fall into debt
lines: An ambitious claim may need time before a decisive test becomes possible.
The book asks whether that interval buys learning or merely extends the protective story.
Evidence debt grows when confidence outruns what a project can presently substantiate.
A corrigible founder preserves channels through which unwelcome findings can change the plan.
The distinction concerns how belief behaves under pressure, not whether ambition looks unusual.

title: Judge before the outcome
lines: Success can make earlier recklessness look wise, while failure can erase a responsible experiment.
The book therefore separates outcomes from the quality of decisions available beforehand.
It asks who could challenge the claim and who would bear the losses.
A failed venture is not automatically fraud or evidence of psychological pathology.
These distinctions make its organizational cases useful without reducing them to stories about exceptional personalities.

title: A test must be allowed to matter
chapter: A test must be allowed to matter
lines: Begin with the nonclinical definition and the distinction between confidence and resistance to correction.
Then follow the cases alongside questions about evidence, dissent, reversibility, and distributed costs.
The practical chapters propose explicit tests, records, and protected routes for unwelcome information.
Their value depends on whether findings can actually change a consequential decision.
Read Too Convinced to Stop to examine ambition before hindsight decides which story everyone tells.
